# Yashvardhan Singh

> Yashvardhan Singh is a VLSI and ASIC design engineer from India. He is a B.Tech student in Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design & Technology) at Manipal Institute of Technology (MIT Manipal), class of 2027, currently on a year-long Digital IP Platform Design internship at STMicroelectronics in Greater Noida. He co-founded ChipMIT, India's first student-run chip design club. His interests are hardware acceleration, digital ASIC design, open-source silicon, machine learning for EDA, and spintronics (CMOS-MTJ).

Homepage: https://yashv373.github.io/
Email: yvs.373@gmail.com
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/yvs373
GitHub: https://github.com/yashv373
Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=YZYt6oYAAAAJ

## Current role
- Digital IP Platform Design Intern, STMicroelectronics (MDRF group), Greater Noida, Jul 2026 to present. Frontend platform work: derivative RTL design, IP-XACT IP packaging, RTL subsystem extraction, SoC assembly and integration, TCL and Python automation.

## Education
- B.Tech, Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design & Technology), Manipal Institute of Technology, Manipal, 2023 to 2027.

## Publications
- Comparative Analysis of Sense Amplifier Circuits for Hybrid CMOS-MTJ CIM Architecture. Yashvardhan Singh (first author), Siddharth Penumatsa, Prashanth Barla. IEEE Journal on Exploratory Solid-State Computational Devices and Circuits (JXCDC), 2026. https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11506373
- ASCON-128a AEAD accelerator with an AXI4-Lite interface in GF180MCU. RS Tarun (IIIT Bangalore), Lakshmi Iyer (IIT Bombay), Yashvardhan Singh. Submitted to IEEE ICEE 2026 (under review). Code: https://github.com/yashv373/ascon128
- Exploring Dopant Choice in HfO2 FE Layer for Negative Capacitance Junctionless FinFET Based Sensors through Sentaurus TCAD. Yashvardhan Singh and Megh Giri. Research Square preprint, 2025. https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-7896806/v1
- Spintronic Cryptography: CMOS-MTJ Hybrid Circuits for Secure Storage Infrastructure. Yashvardhan Singh. SSRN preprint, 2025. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5611750
- Semicustom Frontend VLSI Design and Analysis of a 32-bit Brent-Kung Adder in Cadence Suite. Yashvardhan Singh. arXiv preprint, 2025. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18070

## Selected projects
- ASCON-128a crypto accelerator (2026): AXI4-Lite encryption IP taken RTL-to-GDSII on GF180MCU with LibreLane; timing closed at 16 MHz across corners, DRC/LVS clean; tapeout approval at the IEEE SSCS PICO Chipathon 2026. Built with RS Tarun (IIIT Bangalore) and Lakshmi Iyer (IIT Bombay).
- Project Kalki (2025-26): 4x4 systolic array MAC accelerator for NPUs, RTL-to-GDSII on SkyWater 130 nm with OpenLane; 2.385 mW at 100 MHz, 1.49 pJ/MAC; won Silicon Sprint 2025.
- 32-bit Brent-Kung adder (2025): semicustom Cadence design and comparison with other prefix adders; cited by other researchers.

## Past experience
- Undergraduate Researcher, MIT Manipal, with Dr. Prashanth Barla (2024-2026): spintronics-based ASICs, CMOS-MTJ sense amplifiers.
- Entrepreneur in Residence and Hardware Intern, Ecosight Technologies / BeePrecise, Bangalore (2025): PCB design, 4G SIM module, nRF52840 firmware protection.
- Summer Research Intern, IIT (BHU) Varanasi, with Prof. Shivam Verma (2024): hybrid CMOS-MTJ circuits.

## Leadership
- Co-founder of ChipMIT (Dec 2024); President Apr 2025 to May 2026; now on its Advisory Board. Led Silizium 2026, a 3-day semiconductor summit, and ran events with Marvell.
